overview: Over the last 10 years of chain analysis, we have partnered with law enforcement and industry to disrupt some of the largest threats to our national security and public safety. In these networks and that the majority of the activity is legitimate we do see though that when it comes to threats for example with fentanyl or pig butering or terrorist financing the industry comes together with law enforcement to collaborate on solving these cases and we are chain analysis have powered thousands of investigations that have spanned international geographies cross national boundaries to be able to actually capture criminal proceeds. And we need to bring some clarity to this question of when is the use of digital technology turned something into a security or commodity but that's much more complicated if you will then simply writing in you know a single definition and that's why I advocated process that's why Jake Clayton and I advocated more of a process of bringing the SEC and the CFTC together you don't necessarily have to merge them but we need to have them work together on this. I appreciate it and for that reason I understand we're all concerned about the scams and the fraud that could occur that quite honestly always occurs with some sort of new technology or something happening at the federal level our goal here is to make sure we're protecting our consumers and giving the regulators and law enforcement the tools and the private sector to go after that and stop that. I would say that there are two levels of tooling that is worthwhile, the committee understanding, which is one is there are actual forensic tools that are being used in investigations where you are looking at very specific transactions of interest that have been flagged either through regulatory reporting or investigations. I think we should keep our focus on the main thing and the main thing is safeguarding investors protecting the marketplace and protecting our nation's security and that should be our objective and that's what I heard mostly here today and I hope that as we move forward on market structure this is just a first step guiding principles we have not put forth legislation yet but as we do so we will do so not as red or blue but those committed to red white and blue.
